newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate inches down on liquidity, news.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate inches down on liquidity, news.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down a marginal 10 basis points at 19.50 percent in early trade on Wednesday due to ample market liquidity coupled with an optimistic backdrop provided by Tuesday's debt pre-payment news, traders said.
"Companies make provisional tax payments in full to the banks, which don't charge commission, but the Finance Ministry allows them to hold funds for three days," a dealer said.
"That makes for surplus liquidity...which stands at about 8 billion pesos," he added.

A fixed-income analyst noted secondary rates were also down on peso firmness in the wake of a Finance Ministry announcement on Tuesday it would pre-pay an entire $6 billion issue of floating-rate bank notes.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 2.1 centavos stronger at 7.9060/7.9090 per dollar in early trade.
Overnight rates on bank paper were meanwhile down 70 basis points at 19.70 percent.
Liquidity of 171 million pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank operations, and an additional 300 million pesos in bills were expected to flow back to the market.
